newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand says IFCT agrees to rescue bank.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand says IFCT agrees to rescue bank.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Sunday that the Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand had agreed in principle to help rescue ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce.

Rerngchai told reporters that IFCT was now studying the business and the financial plans of the troubled bank. "IFCT has agreed in principle to run the BBC. It is now looking at certain details and will make a proposal to the IFCT board," he said.
Officials from the central bank will also help the IFCT with the rescue plan, he said, but did not elaborate on a time frame of the scheme.

BBC is now being run by a government panel after it was taken over in May by the government which saved it from a public run on its deposits following disclosure that the bank held up to 77 billion baht ($2.96 billion) of bad and doubtful debt.

A senior central bank official said earlier this month that the central bank was looking for outside professionals to run the bank and that the bank will hold a shareholder meeting in March to seek approval to replace the government panel with a new team. ($1 = 26 baht)
